newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar retraces to end little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar retraces to end little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices ended near unchanged and well off its highs Monday after an early rally stalled at chart resistance, dealers said.
Solid fund-driven buying drove the market higher early in the day, but the uptrend faltered when nearby March futures failed to clear the previous high of 11.12 cents.
As the buying momentum fizzled, producers and the trade sold the market back toward unchanged, where it drifted for the remainder of the session.
"Fund buying pushed it up to the highs, but it couldn't break through last Friday's high," a trader said.
Front-month March eased 0.01 cent per lb on the day, to 11.07 cents, trading from 11.00 to 11.11. May climbed 0.03, to 11.10, while the outer months rose 0.02 to 0.04.
March's slight premium was well supported early in the day, but the contract slipped into backwardation against May as day traders liquidated long positions.
On the charts, traders noted March's failure to set a new peak after climbing on Friday to 10-week highs, but the tone would remain fairly stable while March held above 10.98 cents, they said.
On the physical front, fresh developments were scarce, dealers said, with operations slow to resume after the Christmas and New Year's holidays.
The day's volume was estimated at a steady 18,805 lots.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
